items.title: 17-year-old Rudresh from Thiruvananthapuram donates organs, offering six people a new lease of life
points: Updated - November 03, 2026 09:20 pm IST - Thiruvananthapuram A seventeen-year-old, who suffered brain stem death following a road traffic accident in the city, departed on Tuesday, after giving six others a new lease of life.
The parents of Rudresh S.R., a Plus Two student at A.M.H.S.S.

Following the consent given by the family, Rudresh’s both kidneys, pancreas, liver, both corneas, and the abdominal fascia and vessels were harvested by medical teams for implanting in others awaiting precious organs for a new chance at life.

One kidney was transplanted in an end-stage renal failure patient at Government Medical College Hospital, Thiruvananthapuram, while the other kidney and pancreas were received by a patient suffering from multi-organ failure at KIMSHEALTH, Thiruvananthapuram.
The corneas were retrieved by the Regional Institute of Ophthalmology, Thiruvananthapuram.

Rudresh was riding a motorbike with his friend along the Karamana–Killippalam road on October 26 night when the driver lost control of the two-wheeler, leaving Rudresh and his friend with critical injuries.

items.title: Mandya RSETI, women’s SHG bag Kaushalya Karnataka awards

The Arasamma Women’s SHG of Keragodu Sanjeevini Federation in Mandya taluk has been selected for the award in the non-farm livelihood category under the National Rural Livelihoods Mission (NRLM).

The awards will be presented at a ceremony at the Ashoka Hotel in Bengaluru on Thursday (November 5).

items.title: Extension of MEMU to Ernakulam raises concerns among Kottayam-Kollam commuters
points: Rail commuters from Kottayam, particularly employees of Mahatma Gandhi University, have opposed the Railways’ decision to extend the Kollam-Kottayam MEMU service to Ernakulam, warning that the move would disrupt a vital evening rail link for hundreds…

The Kerala Gazetted Officers’ Sangh has also criticised the decision, while the Mahatma Gandhi University Employees Union has submitted a memorandum to the Divisional Railway Manager, Southern Railway, seeking the continuation of the 5.40 pm…
Under the revised arrangement, the 66315 MEMU, which currently leaves Kottayam for Kollam at 5.40 p.m, will instead originate from Ernakulam at 5.25 p.m. and reach Kottayam at 6.45 p.m.

items.title: Telangana issues public health advisory amid El Nino conditions, urges safe water use and heat precautions
points: People collect water from a tanker in Sangareddy. | Photo Credit: MOHD ARIF The Telangana health department has issued a public health advisory cautioning people against potential risks associated with El Nino conditions, including prolonged dry spells,…
In an advisory issued on Tuesday, November 3, Director of Public Health and Family Welfare Dr. B.
Ravinder Nayak said the changing climatic conditions could increase the risk of water-borne diseases, heat-related illnesses, malnutrition and mental stress.
The advisory has urged people to boil drinking water for at least one minute or use chlorine tablets and filters, even if the water appears clean.

With temperatures likely to pose health risks, the advisory recommends consuming sufficient water throughout the day and supplementing it with Oral Rehydration Salts (ORS), homemade lemon water or buttermilk with a pinch of salt.

People have been advised to avoid outdoor activities and strenuous work between noon and 3 p.m. and to wear light-coloured, loose-fitting cotton clothes while covering their heads when exposed to direct sunlight.

items.title: KTR helps Telangana woman stranded in Muscat return home after employer deceived her
points: Within a month of assuring her son that he would bring his mother home, Mr. Rama Rao fulfilled his promise.
Ms. Tuppudu Lakshmi, wife of Venkatappa, a resident of Gokafasalwad village in Chief Minister A.
Revanth Reddy’s Kodangal constituency, met Mr. Rama Rao on Tuesday at the party office here and expressed her heartfelt gratitude for ensuring her safe return home from Muscat.
According to Mr. Rama Rao’s office, Ms. Lakshmi had travelled to Muscat on February 27 in search of employment, hoping to support her family.
The agent who had sent her abroad stopped answering her calls and reportedly demanded ₹2 lakh to arrange her return.
Unable to bear his mother’s suffering and desperate to bring her back home safely, her son Raju approached Mr. Rama Rao on September 29 and shared their family’s distressing situation.
Keeping his word, Mr. Rama Rao wrote to the concerned officials and facilitated Ms. Lakshmi’s safe return to India.

items.title: Predictable climate finance, equitable transition on India’s COP31 agenda
points: Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta looks on as Union Environment, Forest and Climate Change Minister Bhupender Yadav virtually inaugurates 13 new Continuous Ambient Air Quality Monitoring Stations (CAAQMS).

(Photo: X/@byadavbjp) Predictable climate finance, technology transfer, and nationally determined approaches to climate mitigation and adaptation will comprise India’s key demands at the upcoming UN Climate Change Conference (COP31).

These emerged at a press conference convened by Union Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav on Tuesday (November 3, 2026), outlining India’s priorities ahead of the November 9-20 conference in Antalya, Turkey.
Climate finance will be a central negotiating issue, with India seeking a decision to begin a Climate Finance Work Programme, a pathway mooted at COP 30 in Belém, Brazil, to operationalise this.

Mr. Yadav said finance provided by developed countries under Article 9.1 of the Paris Agreement must be “predictable, largely public and concessional”, and must not add to the debt burden of developing countries.

items.title: Israel opposition backs Gadi Eisenkot for PM, vows to replace Netanyahu's ‘October 7 government’
points: Israel's opposition parties have agreed to rally behind Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot as their candidate for prime minister, setting in motion efforts to form the next government and end Benjamin Netanyahu's tenure.

The leaders of the Change bloc reached the agreement during a meeting in Herzliya, where they discussed using their majority in the newly elected 26th Knesset to establish the country's 38th government.
They also decided to recommend Eisenkot to President Isaac Herzog for the first mandate to form the next government.
In their joint statement, the leaders described Netanyahu's administration as the '7/10 government' and said they would work together to establish a new government at the earliest.

The meeting was attended by Yashar chief Gadi Eisenkot, B’Yachad leader Naftali Bennett and his party's number two Yair Lapid, Yisrael Beytenu leader Avigdor Liberman and Democrats chairman Yair Golan, The Times of Israel reported.

People can burst firecrackers only between 6 a.m. and 7 a.m. and 7 p.m. and 8 p.m. on Deepavali, the TNPCB said in a statement.

Kevin Cormier, Navy’s deputy portfolio acquisition executive, said that the aircraft carrier will be remembered for its legacy, made possible by the sailors and support personnel whose dedication always kept it mission ready throughout her career.
Designated CVN-65, the ship was commissioned in 1960 and entered service the following year as the first nuclear-powered aircraft carrier in the world and a symbol of fine U.S naval engineering.
The former USS Enterprise was part of many important operations which took place during the Cuban Missile Crisis to beyond the Iraq War.

items.title: Norway Detains Sanctioned Chinese Vessel Over False Flag Registration
points: Ya Qing Hai Yang off Vesterålen Islands.

(Courtesy of Arctic North Adventures) Norway has detained a Chinese-owned heavy-lift vessel sanctioned for its role in delivering equipment to Russia’s Arctic LNG 2 project, in what appears to be the first known detention in the Arctic of a Chinese vessel…
The Ya Qing Hai Yang was detained after Norwegian inspectors found that it lacked valid flag-state registration and required certificates, the Norwegian Maritime Authority said.
The Norwegian Maritime Authority inspected the vessel on October 13 after it sought shelter from bad weather in Andfjorden, off the Vesterålen Islands in northern Norway.

“During the inspection, it was discovered that the vessel did not have a valid flag registration and lacked the required certificates,” Dag Inge Aarhus, the authority’s communications director said last week.
“The vessel has therefore been detained until further notice.” The vessel remains off the Vesterålen Islands as of November 3.
